targetAudience.primary: Architects and operators of governed digital employees with multiple credential or execution modes
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands credentials, provider APIs, local runtimes and preflight checks.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A valid worker can be rejected by an irrelevant dependency, or a technically usable route can be mistaken for business authority.

whyNow: A clean-machine failure and merged correction expose how a universal host probe can deny a provider-valid execution route.

externalHook.description: A provider accepts the API key, yet onboarding fails because the host lacks a CLI used only by another execution lane.

coreProposition: Agent admission should be a lane-bound proof bundle: requirements must be derived from and bound to the selected execution lane, while current business authorization remains a separate decision.

originalValue.description: Separates credential validity, host capability, execution-lane identity and business authorization, then derives a typed proof bundle with freshness and verifier identities.

readerTakeaway: Derive admission requirements from the resolved lane, bind proofs to the route actually used, and re-evaluate business authorization at action time.

supported: A direct API-key route was falsely denied by a subscription CLI probe.
The merged fix re-verifies API keys at the provider boundary and retains the CLI check only for subscription execution.
Tests and a narrow provider mock support the bounded mechanism.
unsupported: Business authorization inferred from provider acceptance
End-to-end proof before the next canary

firstPartyRole.rationale: The argument derives from same-date external research and remains independently useful without first-party projects.

decisionReason: The Research Object supports a distinct, evidence-bounded argument with practical governance value.
